phase: Built · milestones 1 to 10 of 11; the last one needs your accounts and a phone
summary: **Milestones 1 to 10 are built.** Every screen drawn for a family, a couple, a flat and a group of friends is built from its drawing and walked through in a browser, in light and dark, as two or more people where something is private: 648 screens a run. The API has 1127 tests and the app 2490. **Milestone 11, real services and real phones, is prepared and waits for you:** nothing has run on a phone or against a real service. Sign-in, storage, push, email and Journey itself are stand-ins on your own computer, every step to connect the real ones is written down, and the Vault needs an outside review before real passwords go in. Every open question is in one place: [What it does](01-requirements.md#questions-for-you).
next: Run it on your Mac: about 20 minutes to set up, then one command. The steps are in `docs/08-run-locally.md` in the repository. Sign in as nora@example.com with the code 123456.
Read the questions in [What it does](01-requirements.md#questions-for-you): seven things only you can do before real people use it, nineteen product decisions, and the calls I made while building.
Say whether I may make the ten changes inside Journey that the link needs (`docs/10-journey-changes.md`). Three of them need a decision from you first.

When you are ready for real services and a build on your iPhone: `docs/09-connect-services.md`, and the checklist for the first build in [the build plan](06-build-plan.md#the-first-build-on-a-phone-what-to-check).

open.q: An outside review of the Vault
open.a: It is built and tested, and its screens say plainly what it protects. A password manager still needs someone outside to try to break it before real secrets go in. The protocol page lists the questions to put to them.

You chose **Homeport** on 12 Nov. It has had a web search, not a legal check: no family app by that name turned up, and US trade mark listings show several HOMEPORT marks, one of them live and one applied for in June 2026 for other software. Have it checked properly, and decide the domain, before the stores. It is one setting if it has to change.

open.q: The accounts, and the first build on a phone
open.a: Nothing has run against a real service or on a phone. The Apple Developer Program and Homeport's own projects at the services Journey uses are yours to set up; every step is written down and none has been run. Face ID, the widgets, the camera and background backup run for the first time on that build, so expect fixes.

The link is built on Homeport's side against a stand-in with two sample journeys. Journey's own code needs ten changes before it is real. Three need a decision first: inviting someone from your circle to a journey without following you, a circle as who can see a journey, and whether the two servers may talk to each other directly.

open.q: Children who use the app themselves
open.a: Built as profiles a parent looks after: nobody under 13 signs in, and what a child ticks is ticked on a parent's phone. Say so if you want children signing in themselves; it brings children's privacy rules with it.

open.q: Reading what you type or say
open.a: “Type it”, Jot, a bill and a school letter are read **by rules on our own side**: right for dates, amounts, names and shopping, rough on anything free-form, and always shown for you to correct. An AI service would read better, costs per use, and the words go to that service. Which do you want?

Only the Vault is scrambled so that the service can't read it. Everything else is private to the people you chose and readable by the service, so that search, reminders from documents and scans work. Photos and scans sit under long random addresses, as in Journey: whoever holds an address can open that file. For passports and bills you may want addresses that expire.

No plans or limits are built. “48 of 200 GB · family plan” is drawn; the 200 GB is a setting and nothing is refused when it is passed. Keeping a family's full-size photos and videos costs roughly US$0.75 to 3 a month per family (worked out for the tech page, not a quote).

Date ideas, Who pays what and Names for couples; Cleaning rota, Bills by nights and Move-in photos for flats. The gallery lists them and each says “Coming with the next update”. Shall I draw and build them, or mark them as later?

Speech to text, the weather, the phone's location, mail forwarded in, a leak check for passwords, a map, reading a scan with the camera, recording inside the app. Each needs a service or a library chosen. Tell me which matter first.

Smaller decisions (what Today lists, one tick for a chore that is also a reminder, On this day, drafts of a journey, what a new account's notifications show) and every call I made while building are in “What it does”, under Questions for you.

updates.text: **Milestone 10, with Journey, is built and tested, and milestone 11 is prepared as far as it goes without your accounts.** With Journey: one account for two apps, keeping a journey as a book with its photos, telling a moment or an album as a journey with a check of every photo before it leaves home, a trip from start to finish, “Alex is on a journey” and On this day on Today, and a goodnight from far away that waits for bedtime. All of it runs against a stand-in for Journey; Journey's own code is untouched. Getting ready: how to run it on your Mac, how to connect each real service, what Journey needs, and the checklist for the first build on a phone are written. The API checks its own settings when it starts and says what is missing. Four faults the last walk-throughs found were fixed: Activity told the API “seen” before the list had answered, so a question that had just come in could lose its “New” mark; a thing that was just deleted was asked for once more while its page closed; a pet was counted among the children when a journey is checked before it leaves home; and the stand-in's pictures did not load. Both QR codes now come from one encoder, which a test holds to another encoder's codes, square for square.

**Milestones 7, 8 and 9 are built and tested.** Fair and fun: whose turn, the piggy bank, secret missions, the Saturday jar, sleeps until, where is it, habit charts. For couples: our story, tucked notes, the anniversary questions, mystery date, both said yes, the fair share. For housemates: the kitty, a fairer split, heads-up, heard in the kitchen, the guest book with its page at the door, everyone who's lived here. For friends: when can everyone (also by link), Secret Santa, where next, the dictionary, predictions, the awards, a goal you walk together. Each kind of circle has its own Today. What is secret stays secret on the other person's phone, and the walk-through checks that as that person. What ties it together: Activity with its filters and asks (allowing one shares the password from your phone), pushes through one outbox that never names what you can't see, the Sunday summary, export, leaving a circle, and deleting the account with “only Homeport, or Journey too”. Two faults the walk-through found on the way were fixed: someone who deleted only Homeport could never come back, and a made-up address said “couldn't read that” in place of “not available”.

**Milestones 5 and 6 are built and tested: Money and the Vault.** Money: bills that repeat with who pays what, reading a bill from its lines, sheets with formulas written as sentences, a row as a card, the loan planner, splitting costs with the fewest payments. Every figure is worked out by the API, so two phones never disagree. The Vault: passwords, cards, IDs, Wi‑Fi and codes scrambled in the app before they leave it; sharing one so someone can use it, see it or change it, once or until a day; the emergency plan with its wait; your Vault key, helpers who can let you back in, and a new phone. The walk-through reads the database as it goes and fails if a password, a key or a passcode is ever there in the clear. Honest limits, also on the screens: Face ID has never run on a phone (a browser uses a passcode), nothing fills a password into other apps yet, no leak check is connected, and the Vault still needs its outside review before real secrets go in. How to run it on your Mac and how to connect the real services are written (docs 08 and 09).

**Milestones 2, 3 and 4 are built and tested: the Library, Plan with Jot, and Notes.** The Library: the wall by day with its years, a moment, the viewer, albums, places, files, a document with its dates, selecting and sharing, storage. Plan: the day's list, the month, events with answers, Type it, reminders with turns and nudges, goals. Jot: the jot bar, what was filed and where, voice (typed in a browser), sharing in, and the widgets, pinned note and Lock Screen written for the phone build. Notes: spaces and folders inside folders, pages made of blocks with live lists, bills and passwords in them, lists that keep working offline and catch up, a page kept as a surprise. With them, the templates gallery and the first ten templates that do work: meal plan, chore wheel, time capsule, and seven keepsakes. What a phone has to do is stood in and says so on the screen: the camera and reading a scan, the microphone, a map, widgets. The walk-through found and fixed several joins between places on the way; one known flaw is left for the next pass: a long list in a browser sometimes reports a harmless layout error.

**Milestone 1 is built and tested.** 24 screens: welcome, sign-in, the setup for each kind of circle, Home with Today, the circle switcher, search, the + sheet, People, a person's page, the audience sheet, a page hidden from one person, guest passes with the guest's own web page, a child's view, You and its settings. The walk-through signs up new people, sets up a family, a couple, a flat and a crew, and checks as a second person that a private page can't be found on Today, in search or by its address until it is shared. 547 app tests and 845 API tests pass. Two faults it found in the API were fixed: a circle with ticked lists could not be deleted, and the web page for Grandma's stories refused its own form.

**The build has started**, on your go-ahead. The app is called **Homeport** everywhere. Done so far: the API's spine (79 tests, among them every way to reach a thing agreeing on who may see it) and the app's foundation from Journey's (225 tests, a walk-through in light and dark).

**The build plan** is written: a new page in this hub and `docs/06-build-plan.md`. Eleven milestones in Journey's way of working (everything on one computer first, real services last), what “done” means for each, how it is tested, six calls for you with the default I'll build, twelve places where the build can't match the drawing, and all 125 screens with their milestone and test level. The hub's build now fails if that list and the screens ever disagree.

**Health is out**, by your decision: the Health place, its eleven screens, and the health details that had crept into other screens (allergies, blood type, vaccination and medical records). The top row is six places again. Two things stayed because they hold no health details: **habit charts** (now in Fair and fun) and **a goal you walk together** (now with the friends' screens, typed in by hand, no link to the phone's health app).

Two decisions from you. **Notes keeps its name**: Lore is gone from every screen. **Health is in the first version**: it now has its own step in the build order, straight after the Vault whose locked storage it uses, and its legal check moves to the top of the next steps.

Three changes you asked for, 37 more screens. **Lore** is the new name for Notes. **Health** (11 screens) is the seventh place, for every circle: who gave the medicine, a sick day written down, the emergency card, moving together, and more. **A circle's kind** now shapes what it gets: two new setup screens, and a full set each for **couples**, **housemates** and **friends** (8 screens apiece: their Home, their templates, three keepsakes, three small rituals).

After your first three comments: 22 more screens. **Jot** (8): widgets, a note pinned in notifications that you type into, voice, the share button, and how each phone's limits are handled. **Keepsakes** (7): Open when…, the birthday interview, Things they said, Same spot every year, Grandma's stories, the good things jar, the doorframe. **Fair and fun** (6): Whose turn?, the piggy bank, secret missions, the Saturday jar, Sleeps until…, Where is it?. Plus *Goodnight from far away* in the Journey group.

First draft: the hub, 75 screens in 13 groups, the design system copied from Journey's Design 2.1, a name shortlist with a switch on every screen, the link with Journey, the requirements, and the answer on sharing a database and a server.
